data.content_ref: inline:SRC_004 inherits from SRC_005 because SRC_005 establishes the behavioral invariant — a typed lease-mismatch code returned before a provider call under a mutated endpoint identity comparison — that SRC_004's temporal mutation (moving the check to post-call) directly violates. The inheritance is that SRC_004's forbidden case (mutating the synchronous precondition to an asynchronous post-provider-call check) presupposes SRC_005's invariant as the baseline the mutation breaks: without SRC_005's typed-code-before-provider-call assertion, SRC_004's temporal mutation has no observable failure to catch, because there would be no typed code whose absence after the provider call signals the temporal violation. The causal mechanism is that SRC_005's invariant creates the signal, and SRC_004's mutation destroys it, so SRC_004's forbidden case depends on inheriting SRC_005's assertion as its detection condition. This claim is REFUTED IF SRC_004's temporal mutation is detectable by a different invariant — such as directly asserting the provider call was never invoked — that does not require SRC_005's typed lease-mismatch code, meaning no inheritance of the detection condition is necessary.
